title: Inside the AI Chip War: From Nvidia’s Dominance to Intel’s Turmoil | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 28

metadata.title: Inside the AI Chip War: From Nvidia’s Dominance to Intel’s Turmoil | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 28

summary: Stacy Rasgon separates the AI semiconductor boom from the weaker analog cycle, stresses NVIDIA's software ecosystem, and remains cautious about AMD and Intel. Eisman tests funding and return assumptions without declaring AI useless or predicting an imminent collapse. The clearest direct correction is that the announced NVIDIA investment in OpenAI was staged. The guest's claim that outsiders do not use TPUs is contradicted by Google's documented multi-year Anthropic relationship.
assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman interviews Stacy Rasgon. Most sector calls belong to Rasgon; Eisman probes returns and valuation and accepts the staged-investment correction.
framework_points: Distinguish economic usefulness from returns on invested capital.
Separate cyclic digestion from a failed structural thesis.
Treat capex cuts as potentially late signals and monitor underlying use.
Do not infer equity value from TAM times assumed share.
Distinguish liquidity support from operating competitiveness.
Demand differentiated customer preference rather than a second-source narrative.
tools_and_charts: GPU versus ASIC share and workload economics
TI inventory days and backlog visibility
Intel foundry losses and external customer milestones
transcript_cautions: All 2009 caption lines were read, including a reread of an initially truncated middle segment.
Guest numbers and management targets are not automatically Eisman forecasts.
Transcript occasionally garbles chip names and semiconductor terms.
The guest immediately self-corrects the lithography size direction; it is not a substantive mistaken thesis.

evidence.title: Intel 2024 Form 10-K
evidence.finding: Foundry operating loss was $13.408 billion in 2024, including substantial impairments, accelerated depreciation, ramp and startup costs. It is not all cash burn or all idle capacity.

evidence.finding: 18A-P entered risk production in June 2026. Q3 external foundry revenue $411 million versus $32 million, mainly a nonrecurring contract, and internal advanced-node volumes increased. External revenue is not necessarily recurring leading-edge wafer volume.
